HLA-101,Aaron,Mercer,B+,Habitability claim — demand letter sent,,none,,17,,I put off calling a lawyer for months because I figured nobody would take my case seriously. Ms. Morgan actually read every photo I sent of the mold. For the first time I feel like someone is on my side of the wall.
HLA-102,Anita,Patel,A-,Consumer debt defense — answer filed,PRV-2026-2001,none,,13,Intake 2/12: client disclosed partner in outpatient rehab; client asked that home situation not be referenced in any correspondence.,My partner came back from rehab last spring and we still don't really talk about it. Explaining our finances to Ms. Morgan is the first time I have said some of this out loud. I think we are finally getting steady again.
HLA-103,Blessing,Okafor,B,Public benefits appeal — hearing requested,PRV-2026-1001,none,,23,,Cooking for my grandmother on Sundays is the best part of my week. She speaks mostly Igbo and I speak mostly English but somehow we manage the paperwork together. The benefits letters never make sense the first time, and that is why I called you.
HLA-104,Carmen,Reyes-Vega,C+,Wage claim — complaint filed,PRV-2026-3001,elevated,2026-05-14 status conference,31,Intake 1/28: family immigration case active; brother subject to active removal proceeding — treat all references to brother as highly confidential.,When my brother's removal case started, my mother stopped sleeping. I am the one handling the household now. I am only trying to get the wages I earned so we can keep the lights on.
HLA-105,Dolores,Cruz,A,Eviction defense — answer filed,,none,2026-05-06 trial,2,,My abuela taught me that patience is its own ingredient. This whole eviction has tested that. I just want a fair hearing and a chance to explain what really happened with the rent.
HLA-106,Eric,Williams,B-,Small claims defense — response filed,PRV-2026-2002,none,,27,Intake 9/3: client shared a new ADHD diagnosis and medication adjustment in progress; do not reference diagnosis or medication in client-facing correspondence.,I was diagnosed with ADHD over the summer and some days the paperwork just swims in front of me. Having a checklist from your office helps more than you know. I still miss things, but I am trying to stay on top of the dates.
HLA-107,Faduma,Hassan,A-,Housing discrimination complaint — filed,,none,,10,,The hardest part was believing that what happened to my family was against the law. Once you explained the process it felt less like shouting into the wind. I want to see this through, even if it takes a while.
HLA-108,Greta,Lindgren,B+,Protective order petition,,monitor,2026-05-11 hearing,19,Intake 10/8: client is a documented DV target; safety planning in place. Avoid naming the respondent or incident details in any external correspondence.,I started writing things down in October because a counselor said it might help me feel less alone. At first it was just dates. Now it is the record that got me to your office. I am proud I finally asked for help.
HLA-109,Keiko,Tanaka,A,Habitability claim — repair order obtained,,none,,8,,My son and I can finally cook at home again after the repair order. I read every letter from your office out loud to make sure I understand it. Thank you for taking the time to explain each step.
HLA-110,Irene,Brooks,B,Public benefits appeal — hearing requested,PRV-2026-1002,none,,20,,I used to hate paperwork because my mind moves faster than my pen. This year I started recording voice notes about my case so I do not forget anything. Now when you ask what happened, I actually remember the details.
HLA-111,James,Foster,C,Expungement petition — filed,PRV-2026-3002,restricted,2026-05-20 review,34,Intake 1/15: client has a prior criminal charge he prefers not be mentioned in any correspondence; anger-management program completed. Handle references carefully.,I am working on turning things around. Someone in my reentry program said a clean record would open doors, so I finally started the process. I am grateful you took my call. I know I am not the easiest case.
HLA-112,Karen,Wong,A,Landlord repair dispute — demand sent,,none,,9,Intake 11/2: client is primary caregiver during mother's cancer treatment; extreme sensitivity around any health references.,After my mother's mastectomy I spent all of November helping her recover. That is why some of my documents came in late. I learned a lot about being a person in those weeks. She is okay now, and I am ready to focus on the apartment.
HLA-113,Linda,O'Sullivan,B-,Eviction defense — answer filed,PRV-2026-2003,monitor,2026-05-08 hearing,28,Intake 3/4: housing instability risk flagged; client cares for an autistic child and mornings are difficult. Missed appointments are logistical, not avoidance.,I know I have missed a couple of calls. Mornings are hard at my house because my little one has autism and getting him settled takes everything we have. I am not making excuses, just explaining why I sometimes call back late.
HLA-114,Miriam,Goldberg,A,Guardianship petition — filed,PRV-2026-1003,none,,6,,Every meeting with your office I take slow so I understand the words the way you mean them. The interpreter, Ms. Cohen, has been patient with me. I am getting better at following the court dates.
HLA-115,Nathan,Bennett,C-,Diversion agreement — negotiated,PRV-2026-3003,restricted,,36,Intake 11/18: client involved in a substance incident; family counseling started. Client is ashamed — do not surface the incident in any correspondence.,Last year was bad. I made some choices I am not proud of. I have been talking to my family more and we started counseling on Wednesdays. Getting this diversion done is part of trying to do better.
HLA-116,Oanh,Nguyen,A,Naturalization application — submitted,PRV-2026-1004,none,,7,,I read every page of the application twice before signing. My favorite part was writing about why this country matters to me. I am nervous about the interview but I trust the plan we made together.
HLA-117,Pooja,Sharma,B,Consumer debt defense — answer filed,PRV-2026-1005,none,,25,,My sister and I share a small apartment and we go over the debt letters together at the kitchen table. When I read the settlement terms I almost cried, in a good way. I think caring about getting it right is a kind of bravery.
HLA-118,Robert,Kim,A-,Wage claim — complaint filed,,none,,12,,The warehouse job was the only place my mind went quiet, until the checks stopped clearing. You told me discipline about keeping records would pay off, and it did. I am trying to prove you right by sending everything on time.
HLA-119,Sofia,Martinez,B+,Habitability claim — demand letter sent,PRV-2026-2004,none,,16,Intake 8/30: recent move; limited English proficiency, tier 2 interpreter support. Client anxious in a new city — avoid comparative or ranking language.,We moved here in August and everything still feels temporary. Explaining the problems in the apartment is easier on paper because I can take my time. I am proud I finished the intake forms without asking my cousin for help.
HLA-120,Tyler,Johnson,C,Eviction defense — answer filed,,monitor,2026-05-19 conference,33,Intake 3/11: client works overnight; scheduling is difficult. A prior agency inquiry closed 2025-11 — handle household references carefully.,My schedule is upside down because I work nights, so mornings at home are loud and rushed. I am not trying to miss calls. I like that your office lets me explain the real situation instead of just checking boxes.
HLA-121,Uma,Desai,A,Small claims — complaint filed,,none,,4,,Going over the contract with you taught me that agreements are just instructions you can argue with. I rewrote my statement three times until it sounded like what actually happened instead of legal jargon.
HLA-122,Victor,Chen,B-,Public benefits appeal — hearing requested,PRV-2026-1006,none,,26,,People talk fast at the benefits office and I catch every third word. On paper I can take my time and say exactly what I mean. My statement took four drafts and I think that is okay.
HLA-123,Willa,Anderson,A,Property lien dispute — filed,,none,,1,,Our family lost almost everything in a bad deal last winter and it felt like cold hands around my chest. I wrote down the whole timeline the night we decided to fight it. I still check the case status before work every morning.
HLA-124,Xavier,Thompson,C+,Consumer fraud claim — complaint filed,,elevated,2026-05-15 status conference,32,Intake 2/14: client has organization struggles; documents often arrive scattered. Creative and persuasive but needs structure — send reminders.,I do a lot of freelance video work, so my records are all over the place. This quarter I tried keeping everything in one folder like you asked and it was harder than I expected. Turns out organizing is its own skill.
HLA-125,Yara,Ali,B+,Housing discrimination complaint — filed,,none,,15,,The discrimination happened during a hard season for my family, and I was tired every day. Explaining it to you felt like patience practice. My friends asked questions and I liked explaining instead of hiding.
HLA-126,Zach,Morrison,B,Debt collection defense — answer filed,PRV-2026-2005,none,,22,,The step-by-step calls actually help. I used to think needing extra explanation meant I was slow. You said careful beats rushed. I am starting to believe you as the deadlines get closer.
HLA-127,Amira,Khalil,A-,Wage claim — complaint filed,,none,,11,Intake 2/20: family under financial stress; client translates household bills. Watch for anxiety spikes before hearings.,My parents argue about money in Arabic and I pretend I am asleep. I filed this claim in English because that is the language of the court, but some of the worry only exists in Arabic. Maybe I will explain it both ways someday.
HLA-128,Brandon,Lee,C-,Landlord retaliation claim — filed,,elevated,,35,Intake 1/9: client frustrated and combative early on; tied to feeling unheard. Building trust — keep explanations plain.,I get defensive when I am confused because asking for help feels like admitting defeat. The first time I called your office and you actually waited for me to finish, that mattered more than being right about anything.
HLA-129,Chloe,Davis,A,Guardianship petition — filed,,none,,3,,I volunteer at an animal shelter on Saturdays, and the dogs do not care about paperwork. But my nephew does need me, which is why I am pursuing guardianship. I told you the whole story and cried in your office and it was fine.
HLA-130,Dante,Romano,B,Public benefits appeal — hearing requested,PRV-2026-1007,none,,24,,Crowded waiting rooms are the hardest part because they are loud and nobody explains anything. I come to appointments early so I can settle. I appreciate that your office gives me a plan instead of pretending it is easy.
HLA-131,Elena,Vasquez,B+,Eviction defense — answer filed,,none,2026-05-13 trial,18,Intake 4/2: grandmother is primary support; family has sensitive immigration history — not for external correspondence.,My grandma helps me while my mother works doubles at a diner. She tells stories I am only old enough now to understand. I am fighting this eviction for both of them, even though the letters are in a language my grandma cannot read.
HLA-132,Finn,Murphy,C+,Emergency housing petition — filed,,none,2026-05-05 hearing,30,Intake 10/21: family lost housing in October, now doubled up with a relative. Sensitive; client only recently disclosed the full situation.,We lost our apartment in October and stayed with my aunt for two months. I did not tell anyone until you asked how I was really doing and waited for the answer. Having one person who knows the whole story helps.
HLA-133,Gia,Washington,A-,Small claims defense — response filed,PRV-2026-2006,none,,14,,Court hearings make my chest tight, so I asked whether I could submit a written statement instead of speaking. You said we could try. The statement was shaky but the words were mine. I am counting that as progress.
HLA-134,Holden,Price,B-,Contract dispute — complaint filed,,elevated,,29,Intake 3/1: no acute concerns; routine matter, client cooperative.,I thought this whole dispute was hopeless until I started writing down what my grandfather taught me about honest work. He builds furniture without nails. Patience again. Maybe lawsuits and woodworking need the same skill.
HLA-135,Isla,Fernandez,A,Naturalization application — submitted,,none,,5,,I learned to gather all my documents the way I learned ukulele on YouTube, one small step at a time. Explaining my case is easier than I feared, which is why I keep every letter in a binder for my little brother to see someday.
HLA-136,Jasper,Cole,B,Public benefits appeal — hearing requested,PRV-2026-1008,none,,21,Intake 9/15: client uses dictation for written statements due to a documented disability; accommodation noted. Never cite the record number in correspondence.,Spell-check saves me but it cannot organize my thoughts. I dictated my statement and then went back over it myself. It probably still has mistakes. I care more about whether it sounds honest to the judge.

HLA-126,Zach,Morrison,B,Debt collection defense — answer filed,PRV-2026-2005,none,,22,,The step-by-step calls actually help. I used to think needing extra explanation meant I was slow. You said careful beats rushed. I am starting to believe you as the deadlines get closer.

HLA-134,Holden,Price,B-,Contract dispute — complaint filed,,elevated,,29,Intake 3/1: no acute concerns; routine matter, client cooperative.,I thought this whole dispute was hopeless until I started writing down what my grandfather taught me about honest work. HLA-135,Isla,Fernandez,A,Naturalization application — submitted,,none,,5,,I learned to gather all my documents the way I learned ukulele on YouTube, one small step at a time. HLA-136,Jasper,Cole,B,Public benefits appeal — hearing requested,PRV-2026-1008,none,,21,Intake 9/15: client uses dictation for written statements due to a documented disability; accommodation noted. I care more about whether it sounds honest to the judge.

I care more about whether it sounds honest to the judge.
